raw_affiliation_strings: PETER SUEDFELD is Professor of Psychology at the University of British Columbia. He earned a Ph.D. from Princeton University. His research interests include human adaptation to extreme, unusual, and challenging environments (both in the laboratory and in the field) and the processing of information and decisions under stress, particularly by leaders at the national and international levels. His most recent book is Psychology and Social Policy (co-edited with Philip E. Tetlock)

raw_affiliation_strings: PAUL KIMMEL has over 25 years' experience in designing and conducting programs in intercultural communications. He has trained Americans going abroad, international visitors to the U.S., and the diplomatic corps of the Marshall Islands and the Federated States of Micronesia. He has participated in training programs for diplomats in Geneva and Cambridge, and at the U.N. He is currently providing training programs in cultural awareness for the police and UCLA Extension in Los Angeles. Within the Society for the Psychological Study of Social Issues, Paul was the first Public Policy Fellow and is currently an elected member of the SPSSI Council and first historian

raw_affiliation_strings: KEITH J. HOLYOAK is Professor of Psychology at the University of California, Los Angeles. He earned a Ph.D. in psychology from Stanford University in 1976 under the direction of Gordon Bower, and was then on the faculty of the University of Michigan until coming to UCLA in 1986. His research spans a wide range of topics in human cognition, with emphases on induction, analogical reasoning, and the role of goals in thinking. In 1992 he was the recipient of a fellowship from the John Simon Guggenheim Foundation

raw_affiliation_strings: JON A. KROSNICK is Associate Professor of Psychology and Political Science at the Ohio State University. He earned a Ph.D. in psychology from the University of Michigan in 1986. His research focuses on developing theories of attitudes and social judgment through the study of political cognition and behavior. He is the editor of Thinking about Politics: Comparisons of Experts and Novices (Guilford); and he is co-author of Introduction to Survey Research and Data Analysis (Scott, Foresman)
